chapter.name: Fundamental Duties
chapter.blurb: Origin, the eleven duties of Article 51A, comparison with Fundamental Rights, enforcement, cases and committees.

scope_in.item: Origin and the eleven duties of Article 51A

scope_out.item: Minerva Mills and M.C. Mehta year claims
scope_out.reason: doubtful in the notes; contradicted by settled law

concepts.name: Fundamental Duties: Part IV-A, Article 51A, enforcement and committees
concepts.description: Origin of Part IV-A, the eleven duties, the contrast with Fundamental Rights, non-justiciability, cases, the Verma Committee and the NCRWC.
concepts.idea: Duties are non-justiciable moral and civic obligations inserted in 1976 and extended in 2002, enforceable only through ordinary legislation.
concepts.rule: Fundamental Duties were inserted in 1976 by the 42nd Amendment Act as Part IV-A, a single Article 51A, on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation and with the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR as the model; the Committee suggested eight duties, ten were enacted and the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added an eleventh (clause k, education of children aged 6-14). Clauses (a) to (k) cover respect for the Constitution, freedom-struggle ideals, sovereignty, defence, harmony and women's dignity, composite culture, environment, scientific temper, public property, excellence and education. Rights are justiciable, individual-centric and mostly negative; duties are non-justiciable, society-centric and mostly positive, yet Parliament may enforce them by law and courts may use them to interpret laws (Mohan Kumar Singhania 1991, Ramlila Maidan 2012). The Verma Committee (1999) identified existing laws giving effect to duties; the NCRWC (Venkatachaliah) urged awareness, sensitising on voting and taxes, and early implementation of the Verma recommendations.
concepts.example: A law such as the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 gives legal teeth to the duty of respecting the National Flag and Anthem.

questions.q: The Fundamental Duty that casts an obligation on a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to a child or ward between six and fourteen years of age was inserted by the
o: 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 along with the original list of duties
questions.e: Clause (k) of Article 51A was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002, as the eleventh duty; it complements the Right to Education under Article 21A.
w: The 42nd Amendment inserted only ten duties in 1976; the educational duty came later.
The 44th Amendment (1978) undid several 42nd Amendment changes but added no duty.
The 93rd Amendment (2005) dealt with reservation in private educational institutions, not with this duty.

questions.q: The idea of embedding a list of citizens' duties alongside rights in the Indian Constitution was drawn from the
questions.a: Constitution of the erstwhile Soviet Union
o: Constitution of the erstwhile Soviet Union
Bill of Rights of the United States
Irish Constitution of 1937, the source of the Directive Principles
questions.e: The Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A, inserted by the 42nd Amendment on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation) follow the model of the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR; the Fundamental Rights, by contrast, are linked to the U.S. Bill of Rights. The Constitutions of the USA, Canada, France, Germany and Australia contain no comparable list of duties.
w: The U.S. Bill of Rights is the inspiration for rights, not duties; the USA has no list of citizens' duties.
The Irish Constitution is the source of the Directive Principles, not of the duties.
The Weimar Constitution is the source of the emergency provisions, not of the idea of listing duties in the Indian Constitution.

questions.q: The number of Fundamental Duties suggested by the Swaran Singh Committee and the number actually placed in Article 51A by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, were respectively
questions.e: The Committee suggested eight duties but the 42nd Amendment included ten; the eleventh came in 2002. The Committee's recommendations on penalties and a duty to pay taxes were not accepted.
w: Reversed: the Amendment enacted more duties than the Committee suggested.
Eleven duties were not reached until the 86th Amendment, 2002.
The Committee did not suggest eleven; the count of eleven is reached only in 2002.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the duties listed in Article 51A of the Constitution?
questions.a: To pay taxes in accordance with law
o: To pay taxes in accordance with law
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform
To value and preserve the rich heritage of the country's composite culture
questions.e: Article 51A has no duty to vote or pay taxes; the Swaran Singh Committee had suggested a tax duty that was not accepted and the NCRWC wanted citizens sensitised about voting and taxes. The other three are clauses (i), (h) and (f).
w: Clause (i) of Article 51A.
Clause (h) of Article 51A.
Clause (f) of Article 51A.

questions.q: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution, which examined Part IV-A and urged awareness of duties through education, media and public campaigns, was chaired by
questions.e: The NCRWC was headed by Justice M.N. Venkatachaliah; it saw duties as tools for democratic behaviour and recommended that Union and State governments spread awareness. Justice J.S. Verma headed the 1999 committee on Fundamental Duties.
w: Justice J.S. Verma headed the separate Verma Committee on Fundamental Duties (1999), not the NCRWC.
Swaran Singh headed the 1976 Congress committee behind Part IV-A.
Justice R.S. Sarkaria headed a commission on Centre-State relations, not the NCRWC.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the origin of Part IV-A of the Constitution:

1. Fundamental Duties were incorporated in the Constitution in 1976 by the 42nd Amendment Act.
2. Part IV-A consists of a single Article, Article 51A.
3. The insertion followed the recommendations of the Verma Committee.
4. The Soviet Constitution inspired the idea of listing citizens' duties.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: 1976, 42nd Amendment. Statement 2 is correct: The new part carries only Article 51A. Statement 3 is incorrect: It followed the Swaran Singh Committee; the Verma Committee came in 1999. Statement 4 is correct: USSR inspiration.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about duties under Article 51A:

1. Clause (a) asks citizens to respect the Constitution, its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Emblem.
2. Clause (b) asks citizens to cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom.
3. Clause (c) asks citizens to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India, a duty that bears directly on resisting secessionism.
4. Clause (d) asks citizens to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Clause (a) names the National Flag and the National Anthem, not the Emblem. Statement 2 is correct: Clause (b) asks citizens to cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom. Statement 3 is correct; the duty to protect unity and integrity bears on resisting secessionism. Statement 4 is correct: Clause (d) asks citizens to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about duties under Article 51A:

1. Clause (e) asks citizens to promote harmony and common brotherhood transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities, and to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
2. Clause (f) asks citizens to value and preserve the rich heritage of the country's composite culture.
3. Clause (g) asks citizens to protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.
4. Clause (h) asks citizens to develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of conformity and tradition.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Clause (e) asks citizens to promote harmony and common brotherhood transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities, and to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women. Statement 2 is correct: Clause (f) asks citizens to value and preserve the rich heritage of the country's composite culture. Statement 3 is correct: Clause (g) asks citizens to protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures. Statement 4 is incorrect: The spirit demanded is of inquiry and reform, not conformity and tradition.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about duties under Article 51A:

1. Clause (i) asks citizens to safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
2. Clause (j) asks citizens to strive for excellence only in scientific and technological activity so that the nation rises to higher levels of achievement.
3. Clause (k) asks a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to a child or ward between six and fourteen years.
4. The Fundamental Duties serve as a warning against anti-national and anti-social activities such as burning the National Flag or destroying public property.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 51A(i) asks citizens to safeguard public property and abjure violence. Statement 2 is incorrect: clause (j) covers excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity, not only science and technology. Statement 3 is correct: clause (k), added by the 86th Amendment (2002), casts the duty on parents or guardians for children aged six to fourteen. Statement 4 is correct: the duties act as a warning against anti-national and anti-social acts such as burning the National Flag or destroying public property.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties:

1. Fundamental Rights are individual-centric, whereas Fundamental Duties are society-centric.
2. A violation of a Fundamental Duty directly attracts a legal penalty from the courts.
3. Fundamental Rights are contained in Part III covering Articles 12 to 30.
4. Rights protect individual liberty and dignity and are justiciable, whereas duties are moral and civic obligations not directly enforceable by courts.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: table. Statement 2 is incorrect: Violation does not directly attract legal penalty; enforcement is indirect, through legislation. Statement 3 is incorrect: Part III covers Articles 12-35. Statement 4 is correct: (nature and enforceability rows).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the nature of Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties:

1. Fundamental Rights are mostly positive in character, needing active contribution by citizens.
2. Fundamental Duties are mostly positive in character, requiring active contribution by citizens.
3. Fundamental Rights act as a limitation on State power and safeguard democratic freedoms.
4. Rights ensure liberty while duties promote responsibility, and together they sustain constitutional democracy.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Rights are mostly negative, restraining arbitrary State interference; it is duties that are mostly positive. Statement 2 is correct: Fundamental Duties are mostly positive in character, requiring active contribution by citizens. Statement 3 is correct: role row. Statement 4 is correct: summary.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the enforcement of Fundamental Duties:

1. Fundamental Duties are justiciable, unlike the Directive Principles of State Policy.
2. Parliament cannot give effect to Fundamental Duties through ordinary legislation without a constitutional amendment.
3. In Mohan Kumar Singhania (1991) the Supreme Court held that Article 51A can be used to interpret ambiguous laws in order to determine their constitutionality.
4. The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 is the law that prevents insults to the National Flag and the Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: both the Directive Principles and the Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable. Statement 2 is incorrect: Parliament is free to enforce the duties by suitable legislation without any amendment. Statement 3 is correct: in Mohan Kumar Singhania (1991) the Supreme Court allowed the duties to be used as an aid in interpreting ambiguous laws. Statement 4 is incorrect: insults to the National Flag and the Constitution are dealt with by the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971; the Wildlife (Protection) Act prohibits trade in rare and endangered species.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect.
'4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Verma Committee on Fundamental Duties:

1. It was appointed in 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
2. It observed that duties are not mere moral ideals but have legal relevance when supported by legislation.
3. It held that public functionaries are exempt from observing Fundamental Duties because of their oath of office.
4. It identified existing legal provisions that already give effect to some Fundamental Duties.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Verma Committee on Fundamental Duties of Citizens was a 1999 committee, not one appointed in 1976. Statement 2 is correct: it observed that duties are not mere moral ideals but have legal relevance when supported by legislation. Statement 3 is incorrect: it said public functionaries must set an example in observing the duties. Statement 4 is correct: it identified existing laws, such as the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 and the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, which already give effect to some duties.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 4, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC):

1. It was chaired by Justice J.S. Verma.
2. It wanted citizens to be specially sensitised about the duty to vote and the duty to pay taxes.
3. It said industrial and corporate organisations should provide education facilities for the children of their employees.
4. It recommended that Part IV-A be deleted as superfluous.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the NCRWC was chaired by Justice M.N. Venkatachaliah, not Justice J.S. Verma. Statement 2 is correct: it noted that the list omits the duties to vote and to pay taxes and wanted citizens sensitised about them. Statement 3 is correct: it said industrial and corporate organisations should provide education facilities for the children of their employees. Statement 4 is incorrect: it viewed duties as instruments of democratic behaviour, constitutional morality and responsible citizenship, not as superfluous.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect.
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Fundamental Duties:

1. Some of the duties are moral precepts while others are civic duties; cherishing the ideals of the freedom struggle is a moral precept, whereas respecting the National Flag and the National Anthem is a civic duty.
2. Safeguarding public property and family planning are both among the duties listed in Article 51A.
3. Both the Fundamental Rights and the Fundamental Duties are confined to citizens and do not extend to foreigners.
4. The duties largely codify values that already belong to Indian tradition and ways of life.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the duties are of two kinds, moral precepts (cherishing the ideals of the freedom struggle) and civic duties (respecting the National Flag and Anthem). Statement 2 is incorrect: public property is clause (i), but family planning is not a listed duty in Article 51A. Statement 3 is incorrect: some Fundamental Rights extend to all persons, citizens or foreigners; only the duties are confined to citizens. Statement 4 is correct: the duties are widely described as a codification of tasks integral to the Indian way of life. So exactly two are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: statements 1 and 4 are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: statements 1 and 4 are correct, not just one.
'Only three' miscounts: statements 2 and 3 are incorrect, leaving two correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Fundamental Duties and the courts:

1. In Re Ramlila Maidan Incident (2012) the Supreme Court observed that a common thread runs through Parts III, IV and IV-A, so an interpretation of any one of them should weigh its impact on all three.
2. Although the duties are non-justiciable, Parliament is free to give effect to them by suitable legislation, which is one indirect route to their enforcement.
3. The Supreme Court has drawn on the duty in Article 51A(g) to protect and improve the natural environment in the M.C. Mehta environmental litigation, including directions on environmental education in institutions.
4. Indira Gandhi defended the inclusion of duties as a means to establish a democratic balance by making citizens as conscious of their duties as of their rights.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: in In Re Ramlila Maidan Incident (2012) the Supreme Court observed that a common thread runs through Parts III, IV and IV-A, so an interpretation of any one of them should weigh its impact on all three. Statement 2 is correct: the duties are non-justiciable, but Parliament may give effect to them by suitable legislation. Statement 3 is correct: the M.C. Mehta litigation rests on Article 51A(g), the duty to protect and improve the natural environment. Statement 4 is correct: Indira Gandhi defended the duties as a means to establish a democratic balance between rights and duties. So all four are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 4 statement(s) are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 4 statement(s) are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 4 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the NCRWC and the Verma Committee:

1. The NCRWC viewed duties as instruments for democratic behaviour, constitutional morality and responsible citizenship.
2. The NCRWC recommended that the Union and State governments spread awareness of duties through education, media and public campaigns.
3. The NCRWC asked that implementation of the Verma Committee's recommendations be deferred until duties are made justiciable.
4. The Verma Committee said citizenship ethics should be strengthened through education and public conduct.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The NCRWC viewed duties as instruments for democratic behaviour, constitutional morality and responsible citizenship. Statement 2 is correct: The NCRWC recommended that the Union and State governments spread awareness of duties through education, media and public campaigns. Statement 3 is incorrect: It recommended early implementation, especially civic education, ethical governance and leadership accountability. Statement 4 is correct: . So exactly 3 are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Fundamental Duty to provide educational opportunities to children aged six to fourteen was part of the original list of duties added in 1976.
Statement-II: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added that duty, and it complements the Right to Education under Article 21A.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect: the 42nd Amendment (1976) added ten duties; the educational duty was added in 2002 as clause (k). Statement-II is correct: the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added that duty alongside the Right to Education under Article 21A.
w: 'Both correct and II explains I' fails: Statement-I is incorrect because the educational duty is clause (k), added in 2002, not part of the 1976 list.
'Both correct but II does not explain I' also fails: Statement-I is incorrect since the 42nd Amendment gave only ten duties.
'I correct but II incorrect' reverses the verdicts: Statement-II is correct (86th Amendment, 2002).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Fundamental Duties cannot be dismissed as merely symbolic even though they are non-justiciable.
Statement-II: Several existing laws, such as the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, give effect to some of the duties.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both correct. Duties are not directly enforceable by courts, yet the Verma Committee identified existing laws operationalising them, which is why they are not merely symbolic: Statement-II explains Statement-I.
w: Statement-II is the very evidence for Statement-I, so it does explain it.
Statement-II is correct, so 'I correct, II incorrect' fails.
Statement-I is correct, so 'I incorrect' fails.

questions.q:
Match the body or case in List-I with its association in List-II.

List-I
A. Swaran Singh Committee
B. Verma Committee (1999)
C. NCRWC (Venkatachaliah)
D. Mohan Kumar Singhania case (1991)

List-II
1. Suggested that Parliament may impose penalty for non-observance of the duties, a recommendation not accepted in 1976
2. Identified existing laws, such as the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971, that give effect to some duties
3. Said industrial and corporate organisations should provide education facilities for the children of their employees
4. Article 51A may be used to interpret ambiguous laws
questions.e: Swaran Singh Committee: penalty for non-compliance was suggested but not accepted. Verma Committee: existing laws such as the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971. NCRWC: industrial and corporate bodies to provide education facilities for employees' children. Mohan Kumar Singhania: Article 51A to interpret ambiguous laws.
w: A and C are interchanged: the penalty suggestion was the 1976 committee's; the corporate-education recommendation is the NCRWC's.
B and D are interchanged: the case is about interpretation, the Verma Committee listed laws.
Every pair is misplaced; check each body against its own recommendation.
